direction.premise: A minimal sword duel lets each fighter weaponize a delayed recording of their own movement and attacks.
direction.composition: An unobstructed arena occupies the main screen; compact room status sits above it and two input pads sit at the bottom.
direction.shapeLanguage: Cyan and rose circular fighters have visible sword bearings; translucent echo actors repeat the same geometry among rectangular walls.
direction.surfaceAndMaterial: Flat opaque fighters and low-contrast arena walls keep the live sword, shield arc and recorded ghost distinguishable.
direction.paletteLogic: Cyan identifies the local fighter, rose the opponent and translucent blue the delayed actor; pale arcs show weapon direction.
direction.typography: Small system labels name room, mode and four combat verbs without decorative combat text in the world.
direction.signature: A translucent copy replays real recorded inputs while the live fighter can charge a different attack or raise a parrying shield.
direction.distinction: FOG uses geographic orders and ZAMAZKA uses painted restoration fragments; this port retains its source game object and the specific input loop described here.

architecture.primaryVerb: Approach an opponent, charge and release a sword strike, parry incoming attacks and trigger one of three recorded-echo behaviors.
architecture.physicalFeedback: Sword charge changes attack power; a fresh shield can stagger an attacker, while a lethal hit fades the actual fighter before the next round.
architecture.spatialRationale: An unobstructed arena occupies the main screen; compact room status sits above it and two input pads sit at the bottom. This keeps the current game object and its real inputs spatially connected on a phone.

production.renderer: Canvas 2D retains the abstract original duel geometry and keeps ghost history independent from the authoritative live actor.
production.focalAsset: Live and ghost actor silhouettes are rendered from the original engine; the authored crossed-blade icon identifies the three-mode duel.

motion.character: Sword charge changes attack power; a fresh shield can stagger an attacker, while a lethal hit fades the actual fighter before the next round.
motion.action: Approach an opponent, charge and release a sword strike, parry incoming attacks and trigger one of three recorded-echo behaviors.
motion.anticipation: The current selection, room state and available control labels expose the pending operation before the player activates it.
motion.response: The next visible state responds to the actual control: A translucent copy replays real recorded inputs while the live fighter can charge a different attack or raise a parrying shield.
motion.followThrough: The resulting world, board or round state remains visible until a later explicit action changes it; no decorative transition hides the outcome.
motion.interruption: Repeated input uses the current state; pointer cancellation releases held controls and hidden tabs stop transmitting held actions.
motion.reducedMotion: The complete play state remains legible without decorative entry animations; spatial gameplay and authoritative outcomes retain their original timing.

evidence.expectedChange: A private duel room opens with one live fighter and its generated wall map, waiting for the second player.
